blurb: Rustia is a pure-Rust interpreter for embedding standalone [Luau](https://luau.org/) in games and tools. Edit scripts without a rebuild and let players write mods.
origin: We built Rustia at [Slowchop Studios](https://slowchop.com/) for a [Bevy](https://bevy.org/) game. We wanted to tweak gameplay without waiting for Rust to recompile, run scripts quickly and safely, and get deterministic results for multiplayer and replays on desktop and in the browser.
firstScriptIntro: Start with a score of 21 and a Rust function called `double`. The Luau script calls `double(base_score)` and sends 42 back to Rust.

features.title: Hot reload
features.description: Edit Luau without a rebuild. Your app keeps running and can carry state across edits, like the flowers’ positions in the garden. If a reload fails, Rustia can restore the previous script state.

features.title: Deterministic execution
features.description: Replay a run. In deterministic mode, the same script, starting state, seed, and ordered inputs produce matching results on native and WebAssembly. That helps reproduce bugs and keep lockstep multiplayer clients in sync.

features.title: Parallel script execution
features.description: Run independent Luau VMs on Rust worker threads. Each VM has its own script state, and your app schedules the work.

features.title: Pure Rust runtime
features.description: One interpreter on desktop and web. Rustia’s runtime crates forbid `unsafe` Rust and build without a C++ toolchain.

features.title: Sans-I/O core
features.description: Embed Luau without relying on built-in platform services. Your app can supply clocks and randomness, decide where `print` output goes, and choose how to load scripts.

features.title: Rust functions and objects
features.description: Let scripts work with your app. Expose the functions and objects they need, and use Serde to read Luau tables into Rust structs.

features.title: Script execution limits
features.description: Keep runaway scripts under control. Set instruction and VM memory budgets so your app can handle a script that exceeds them.

upcoming.title: Time-travel debugging
upcoming.description: Step back through a recorded Luau run, inspect earlier values, and find the line that last changed a variable. [Follow the debugger work](https://github.com/slowchop/rustia/issues/71).

upcoming.title: A Luau layer for Bevy
upcoming.description: We’re building a Luau layer on top of [Bevy](https://bevy.org/) so you can change gameplay while the game runs, without rebuilding the Rust app.

upcoming.title: JIT and AOT research
upcoming.description: We’re exploring just-in-time (JIT) compilation in the background during development and ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation for bundled scripts. Today Rustia interprets Luau bytecode. [Follow the compilation work](https://github.com/slowchop/rustia/issues/89).

upcoming.title: Synth in Luau
upcoming.description: We’re also having fun with a Luau synth in the browser. Write and tweak sounds live, record MIDI performances, and record audio from instruments.
